questions.stem_text:
You've made a scientific theory that there is an attractive force between all objects.
When will your theory be proven to be correct?

options.A: When the theory can predict future observations.
options.B: As soon as you propose the theory.
options.C: When your theory becomes a law.
options.D: You can never prove your theory to be correct only "yet to be proven wrong".
options.E: When the scientific community accepts it as a fact.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - You can never prove your theory to be correct only "yet to be proven wrong".

questions.stem_text:
A particle of charge $1.8 \mu \mathrm{C}$ is at the center of a Gaussian cube $55
\mathrm{~cm}$ on edge. What is the net electric flux through the surface?
Which statement about an atom is not true:

options.A: A neutral atom always has equal numbers of electrons and protons.
options.B: The electrons can only orbit at particular energy levels.
options.C: Electrons and protons in a neutral atom are always equal in number.
options.D: Electrons can orbit at any energy level.
options.E: A neutral atom always has equal numbers of neutrons and protons.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: E - A neutral atom always has equal numbers of neutrons and protons.
